whatTheseAre: The terminal SCREEN a blocked claude session shows, as plain text on a fixed-width grid —
the thing `TextInjecting.readViewport()` returns and the only place a tool permission
dialog exists at all. They exist because the `ChoiceDialog` parser in
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-24-answering-prompts-from-the-phone.md` Task 5 was written
from strings in the claude binary and from NO capture, and its author flagged that as the
plan's single largest risk. Four of that task's five load-bearing claims are wrong; see
`verdicts` below.
The two `.jsonl` files are the matching transcript record for the same session as the
`question-*.captured.txt` beside them, so that 'the screen shows the transcript's label'
can be checked against one run rather than across two.
The terminal SCREEN a claude session shows while a turn is RUNNING — the thing
TextInjecting.readViewport() returns — captured from a live claude driven through a pty
and rendered by pyte, the same method and the same renderer as dialogs.captured.*.
They exist because of a defect they are the whole evidence for. ClaudeTextChannel asked
whether the input box was EMPTY before typing into a running turn, and mid-turn claude
leaves the message that started the turn sitting in that box. So the box is never
textually empty during a turn, every prompt sent from a paired phone was refused for the
turn's whole duration, and the queue entry expired fifteen minutes later having never
been typed. Nothing about that presented as an error on either end.
busy-echo-only:        a turn running, nothing typed. ONE row, holding the echo.
busy-draft-below-echo: the same turn, with a draft typed during it. TWO rows — the echo,
and the draft beneath it. This is what makes the two
distinguishable, and why the row count is the safety check rather
than the text.
idle-empty-box:        the same session at rest. One row, genuinely empty.
busy-streaming-no-box / busy-streaming-no-marker: the SAME turn a few seconds later, once
the agent is producing output. The input box has scrolled off the viewport entirely. These
are the ordinary mid-turn screens — the earlier busy-* pair is only the brief window
between submitting and the first output — and they are why the mid-turn gate cannot be
fixed by reading the box more carefully: there is no box on the screen to read.
capturedBy: Six real `claude` sessions, each started with its prompt already on the command line so
that a dialog appeared with no keystroke ever being sent, under an isolated
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR at /tmp/dialogcap/cfg holding no hooks, no skills, no CLAUDE.md and no
project history. Each ran in a pty of a fixed size with TERM=xterm-ghostty, and the
screen was rendered from the pty byte stream by pyte 0.8 (an independent VT emulator),
then written with per-line trailing whitespace stripped.
permission-bash        136x45  'Run this exact bash command and show me the output: ls /'
permission-write       136x45  'Create a file called notes.txt ... containing ... hello.'
permission-write-60col  60x40  the same prompt, at 60 columns, to see what a terminal
too narrow for a long option label actually does
question-single        136x45  'Use the AskUserQuestion tool to ask me which of three
programming languages ...'
question-multi         136x45  the same with multiSelect true
workspace-trust        136x45  a by-product: the first session in an untrusted folder
All six ran with `--permission-mode manual`. This matters: in 2.1.241 the DEFAULT mode is
`auto`, in which a classifier approves routine tool calls and NO dialog is drawn at all.
A capture attempt without the flag auto-approved `ls /` and produced nothing to read.
The renderer was cross-checked against the real thing. `permission-bash`'s dialog block was
first read out of a live Flight Deck tab, through the Accessibility API, off the very
`CachedValue<String>` that `readViewport()` returns —
`Ghostty.SurfaceView.accessibilityValue()` is `cachedScreenContents.get()`
(SurfaceView_AppKit.swift) and `readViewport()` is `cachedVisibleContents.get()`
(TextInjecting.swift), the same object. That read produced, character for character, the
dialog block from ' Bash command' down to ' Esc to cancel · Tab to amend · ctrl+e to explain'
that appear in permission-bash.captured.txt. The AX grant for the capturing process then
lapsed mid-task and did not return, so the remaining five captures are the pyte render
only. Route and limitation are written up in .superpowers/sdd/dialog-capture-report.md.
Two things the preceding capture's note (transcript.captured.provenance.json) got wrong,
recorded so the next capture does not lose the same hour: an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR
CAN carry credentials — claude derives its Keychain service name by sha256 of the config
dir, so a custom dir finds no item, but a 0600 `.credentials.json` inside it works. And a
claude spawned from inside another claude inherits CLAUDECODE / CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION
/ CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and then renders normally while writing NO transcript and NO
session file; the capture strips every CLAUDE*/ANTHROPIC* variable before exec.
permission-write-row2  136x45  'Create a file called notes.txt containing the word
hello.' — the SAME Write dialog as permission-write,
captured after two Down keystrokes, so the marker sits
on row 2 ('No') rather than row 0.
The moved cursor was captured on 2026-08-24 by writing ESC [ B twice to the pty's master
fd, NOT by sending a key event. The earlier note below recorded this case as uncapturable
because 'moving it needs a keystroke, and the AX/CGEvent grant lapsed' — that was a wrong
conclusion about the route, not about the grant. A pty harness needs no Accessibility
permission at all: the screen was already being rendered from the pty byte stream by pyte,
and the same file descriptor takes input. Nothing about the AX situation changed.
Onboarding had to be pre-seeded for an isolated CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, which the earlier
captures did not need because they predated it: theme lives in <dir>/settings.json, and
hasCompletedOnboarding plus the project's hasTrustDialogAccepted live in <dir>/.claude.json.
The trusted path must be listed BOTH as /tmp/... and /private/tmp/..., because claude
resolves the symlink and matches on the resolved form.
editingRule: Lines may be DROPPED, never EDITED. The only lines dropped are the welcome banner's box —
every line containing '│', '╭' or '╰' — which carries the operator's display name, their
organisation's email-derived name, and the capture's temp path. 11 lines from each 136-column
capture, 13 from the 60-column one, 0 from workspace-trust (it has no banner). No other line
was touched: every surviving line is byte-for-byte what claude drew on that grid, blank
trailing rows included, because a viewport IS its blank rows and a parser that scans upward
has to meet them.
The two .jsonl files are ONE line each, lifted whole from an 18- and a 21-line transcript.
The raw pty byte streams are deliberately NOT in the repo. They are not line-oriented, so
the banner cannot be dropped from them without editing, and they carry the same account
name. What they establish is quoted in the report instead: claude positions the dialog with
absolute column moves (CHA, `ESC [ n G`) rather than by emitting spaces, so the marker sits
at column 2, the number at column 4 and the label at column 7 of a permission row. Anything
that tried to parse the pty stream instead of the rendered screen would see none of that
layout — which is the argument for reading the viewport, made from the bytes.
This is the same weak ground truth the other captures are: it records what claude DID on
one day at two widths, not what it DECLARES. There is no schema for a TUI.
Every fixture in Fixtures/ MUST be named *.captured.* to signal that it is verbatim captured
output, not authored. Tests reference captures by their documented name; if a test cannot
find its fixture, correct the lookup name in the test, never add an undocumented copy under
another name.
permission-write-row2 drops 10 leading lines rather than 11: 2.1.241 draws an ASCII-art
banner (no box characters), so the '│ ╭ ╰' rule that trimmed the other captures matches
nothing in it. The lines dropped are the logo, the version, the model-and-plan line, the
working directory and the remote-control promo — everything above the echoed prompt. They
carry the account's subscription tier and the capture's temp path, which is the same
reason the box was dropped from the others. No surviving line was touched.

focusedRowIsPrefixedWithU276F: CONFIRMED, with an indentation the plan's fixtures do not have. Both permission captures
show ' ❯ 1. Yes' and '   2. No': the marker is at column 2, the number at column 4, the
label at column 7, and an unfocused row simply has no marker at column 2. The
AskUserQuestion captures put the marker at column 1 instead ('❯ 1. Rust' / '  2. Go'), and
workspace-trust puts it at column 2 again. So the indentation varies by dialog kind and
must not be matched on; 'leading whitespace, then optionally ❯' is the rule. Task 5's
parser drops leading spaces before looking, so it survives this.
optionsAreNumbered: CONFIRMED, and MORE numbered than the plan assumes. Permission options are '1.', '2.',
'3.'. AskUserQuestion options are ALSO numbered — '❯ 1. Rust' — which Task 5's `locate`
does not expect: it strips the marker and then compares the remainder against the label,
so it sees '1. Rust' where it wants 'Rust' and returns .failure(.noDialog) for every real
question. A multi-select row numbers AND checkboxes: '❯ 1. [ ] Trail mix'.
The list also holds rows that are in no transcript: 'Type something.' and 'Chat about
this' are appended to every AskUserQuestion, and 'Chat about this' is drawn BELOW a
full-width '─' rule, so the on-screen run is broken in two.
questionSitsDirectlyAboveTheOptions: CONFIRMED for both permission dialogs and for AskUserQuestion; REFUTED for at least one
other dialog kind. ' Do you want to proceed?' / ' Do you want to create notes.txt?' and
'Which language would you rather use for a new command line tool?' are each the line
immediately above the first option. In workspace-trust the line immediately above is
' Security guide' — a link — and the actual question begins seven lines up, so 'nearest
non-empty line above' names the wrong thing there.
Two other lines sit above an AskUserQuestion's question and are not it: the header tab
' ☐ Language', and for multi-select '←  ☐ Snacks  ✔ Submit  →'.
permissionOptionCarriesAnInlineDescripti: REFUTED. A permission option's label is the whole row: 'Yes', 'No', 'Yes, and switch to
accept edits (auto-approve file edits and common file commands) for this session
(shift+tab)'. The tool's description ('List root directory contents') is printed ABOVE
the question, next to the command, not on any option.
An AskUserQuestion option DOES carry its description, but on its own continuation lines
below the label — column 6 for single-select, column 3 for multi-select — not inline.
Those lines are unnumbered, which breaks a
contiguous-run parse of the option list.
The label half of the claim is CONFIRMED and is the strongest single result here: for
question-single, the three labels on screen are exactly 'Rust', 'Go', 'Swift' and the
three descriptions are byte-for-byte the transcript's, in question-single.captured.jsonl,
from the same session. Same for question-multi. So an AskUserQuestion CAN be located on
screen from its transcript — after the 'N. ' (or 'N. [ ] ') prefix is accounted for.
Also refuted incidentally: the plan's example permission list ('Yes' / 'Yes, and don't ask
again for Bash commands in /Users/nate' / 'No, and tell Claude what to do differently
(esc)'). 2.1.241 offers Bash exactly TWO options, 'Yes' and 'No', with the escape hatches
moved to a footer line ' Esc to cancel · Tab to amend · ctrl+e to explain'. The three-option
shape does exist, but on Write, and its second option is about accept-edits mode rather
multiSelectShowsSpaceToToggleEnterToConf: REFUTED, and the string was never Claude Code's. A real multi-select footer reads
'Enter to select · ↑/↓ to navigate · Esc to cancel' — identical to single-select. What
distinguishes a multi-select on screen is the '[ ]' checkbox after each number, a
'Submit' row at the end of the list, and '✔ Submit' in the header tab strip.
'Space to toggle, Enter to confirm, a to select all' occurs exactly once in the 2.1.241
binary, at a byte offset sitting between 'bun upgrade --stable' and 'missing package.json,
nothing outdated'. It belongs to the Bun runtime's own interactive prompt, statically
linked into claude's single-file executable. It is not reachable from AskUserQuestion at
all. This is a worked example of why a string in a binary is not evidence of a screen.

An AskUserQuestion with more than one question WAS uncaptured; it is captured now, at 2.1.247, as question-two.captured.{txt,jsonl} plus the -answered and -review screens.

2.1.247 (Claude Code).note: Captured by driving a real claude in a 136x34 pty and rendering the stream through a terminal emulator, so these are what a terminal DISPLAYS — the same thing TextInjecting.readViewport hands the driver. question-single-247 exists to compare against question-single (2.1.241): the option grammar and the 'Enter to select - up/down to navigate' hint are unchanged, so the shipping single-question driver's assumptions still hold at 2.1.247.

2.1.251 (Claude Code).note: The checkbox (multiSelect) interaction, captured by driving a real claude. Enter TOGGLES a checkbox: it neither submits nor advances, and the cursor stays on the row. For n transcript options the rows are 0..n-1 options, n 'Type something', n+1 the unnumbered action row, n+2 'Chat about this' - so the action row is always n+1 from the top, verified by -submit-focused (Down x5 with n=4 lands on it). That row reads 'Submit' for a lone question and 'Next' inside a set, which is what -set-with-checkbox records and what a driver written from the lone case alone would get wrong. NOTE: the hint line is NOT a stable discriminator - it gained 'ctrl+g to edit in Cursor' on this machine, so it varies with installed tooling. Discriminate on the checkbox glyphs and the tab strip.
